title: Asyncio coroutine context auto-instrumentation and low-overhead task propagation
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Add an opt-in auto-instrumentation layer in the Python SDK that reliably propagates request/tracing context across asyncio coroutines, async generators, and TaskGroup-style concurrency. The goal is zero-config compatibility for common frameworks (aiohttp, httpx async client, FastAPI/Starlette, and gRPC aio) while keeping overhead <1% p50 latency for typical 50ms RPC calls. This ticket covers design, prototype instrumentation hooks, sampling hints integration, and a staged rollout plan for runtime-1.20.
comments: 2025-01-18 - Aisha Kumar: Initial ticket. Background: customers report missing spans when switching to async code paths (async generators, background tasks). We need an SDK-layer approach rather than framework-specific adapters to reduce maintenance surface. Linked design notes in Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OBS/Async+Context+Propagation+Design

2025-01-22 - Miguel Santos: Spike completed. Prototype uses contextvars + lightweight task-local registry plus an opt-in patch that wraps asyncio.create_task, TaskGroup, and ensure_future. Prototype handles: coroutine entry/exit, async generator yield/resume, and hooking into aiohttp ClientSession._request. Measured overhead: +0.6% p50 on synthetic 50ms RPC benchmark. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/4123

2025-01-30 - Eng Infra (review): Concern about monkeypatching TaskGroup in Python 3.11+ and backport compatibility. Two options: 1) provide decorator-based API for frameworks that want explicit integration; 2) keep runtime auto-patch but expose opt-out switches and robust feature-detection. Decided to implement feature-detection + graceful fallback and comprehensive test matrix across 3.9-3.12.

2025-02-03 - Design review (L. Park): UX for opt-in should be simple: SDK env var REDWOOD_TRACING_ASYNC=auto|explicit|off. Also proposal to surface a small debug endpoint in Redwood Console to show which instrumentations are active per client token for easier support triage.

2025-02-10 - Miguel Santos: Implemented sampling hint propagation using the existing headers format (x-rw-sampling-hint). When starting background tasks, we attach a sampling hint and sticky attribute so downstream work inherits the same sampling decision. Unit tests added for sampling-preservation and for the case where parent context is missing (generates new trace with default sampling). PR updated: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/4123 (force-push after tests)

2025-02-14 - QA (R. Chen): Integration tests flake on CI in pypy environment - contextvars semantics differ. Mitigation: add explicit fallback using weakref-based threadlocal for pypy and add CI job matrix entry for pypy. Filed small follow-up ENG-78075 for pypy resilience.

2025-02-20 - Miguel Santos: Preparing canary. Canary plan: roll SDK 2.7.0-beta with REDWOOD_TRACING_ASYNC=auto to 10% of hosted API tokens for 48h, monitor span coverage, error rates, and client-side latency. Dashboards: create tracing coverage panel and async-span-drop rate (new metric). Rollback criteria: >0.5% absolute increase in 95th percentile client latency or >30% drop in expected child spans for known instrumented endpoints. Console dashboard PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/2139
